title: Components of fitness & tests
examples: Which fitness component measures how strong your muscles are?
Can you tell me a test for endurance?
What is the difference between stamina and strength?

explain.say: Today we are learning about fitness components. These are parts of being physically fit.
Strength is how much force your muscles can exert. A simple example is doing a maximum number of push-ups.
Stamina, or endurance, is how long you can keep exercising. A good test for this is running a set distance.
Flexibility is the range of movement in your joints. We test this by measuring how far you can touch your toes.

draw.text: Flexibility: Joint range (e.g., Sit and Reach)

explain.say: In real life, you use these components every day. For example, climbing many flights of stairs uses your stamina and leg strength.
A common mistake is thinking strength and stamina are the same. Strength is a single burst, while stamina is lasting longer.

faq.q: What is the difference between strength and power?
faq.a: Strength is the maximum force your muscles can exert. Power is the rate at which you can exert that force, combining strength and speed.
asks: How are strength and power related?

faq.q: Do I need to be flexible to be strong?
faq.a: No, you can be strong without being extremely flexible. However, good flexibility can improve your range of motion during strength exercises.
asks: Does stretching help my muscles get stronger?
Is flexibility necessary for lifting weights?

faq.q: What is the best test for cardiovascular fitness?
faq.a: A common test for cardiovascular fitness is the mile run or a timed shuttle run. These measure your heart and lung endurance.
asks: Which test uses running for fitness?

faq.q: How often should I test my fitness components?
faq.a: It is best to test yourself regularly, perhaps every few months. This helps you track your progress and see improvements over time.
asks: Should I test my fitness every year?
How often is it good to check my fitness?

faq.q: What does 'endurance' mean in fitness terms?
faq.a: Endurance means you can perform an activity for a long time without getting too tired. It relates to your stamina.

facts: Strength refers to the maximum force a muscle can generate.
Stamina, or endurance, is the ability to sustain effort over time.
Flexibility measures the range of motion at a joint.
Fitness tests measure these components to track physical health.

quiz.say: If you are trying to improve your ability to run for a long time, which component are you focusing on?
quiz.why: Stamina is specifically about maintaining effort over an extended period of time.

wrong.0: Strength is about how much force you can push or pull at one time.
wrong.1: Flexibility only measures how far your joints can bend.
wrong.2: Power is more about speed combined with force, not just duration.

quiz.say: A sit and reach test is used to measure which component of fitness?
quiz.why: This test directly measures the range of motion in the lower back and hamstrings.

wrong.0: Power requires a quick, explosive action, not just a stretch.
wrong.2: Strength tests involve lifting or pushing against resistance.
wrong.3: Stamina requires continuous movement over a distance or time.

quiz.say: Which fitness component is best tested by doing a maximum number of vertical jumps?
quiz.why: Jumping requires your muscles to exert maximum force quickly, which relates to strength.

wrong.0: Flexibility tests involve passive stretching, not explosive jumping.
wrong.1: Endurance is a general term, but strength measures the peak force capability.
wrong.3: Stamina tests would involve jumping repeatedly for many minutes.
